ai-at-work.title: Apple sues OpenAI over alleged trade secret theft
ai-at-work.excerpt: Apple alleges the misconduct was directed by OpenAI's senior leadership, including a longtime former employee.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Apple is suing OpenAI, claiming the company stole trade secrets with the knowledge of senior leadership, including someone who used to work at Apple. This matters because digital workplace teams need to understand how AI vendors handle confidential information, especially if your organization is integrating these tools into your environment and trusting them with proprietary data. Honestly, this is a good reminder that just because a platform is shiny and popular doesn't mean you've done your due diligence on security and governance before handing over your company's crown jewels.

ai-at-work.title: SK Hynix raises $26.5B in the biggest foreign IPO in US history, is urged to build new US fabs
ai-at-work.excerpt: The AI chip boom just produced its biggest Wall Street moment yet. Now SK Hynix and Samsung are being asked to build U.S. factories.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: SK Hynix just raised $26.5 billion in the largest foreign IPO the US has ever seen, and now there's political pressure for them to build manufacturing facilities stateside. This matters to digital workplace pros because chip supply chain resilience directly impacts hardware refresh cycles, cloud infrastructure costs, and ultimately what tools your organization can actually afford to deploy. Here's the thing: politicians love asking foreign companies to build factories, but SK Hynix will make that decision based on labor costs and tax incentives, not patriotic appeals, so don't hold your breath waiting for that shiny new US fab to suddenly solve your hardware budget problems.

ai-at-work.title: OpenAI is shutting down Atlas, but its AI browser ambitions are still growing
ai-at-work.excerpt: OpenAI is sunsetting its AI-powered browser after less than a year. But it's moving some agentic browsing features to its desktop app and a Chrome extension.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: OpenAI is killing Atlas, its standalone AI browser that barely lasted a year, but shifting those browsing features into ChatGPT's desktop app and a new Chrome extension instead. This matters because it signals where AI automation is actually heading: integrated into tools you already use rather than forcing you to adopt entirely new apps, which means digital workplace teams need to rethink how they manage AI capabilities across existing platforms. Honestly, it's refreshing to see someone abandon a half-baked product instead of shipping it anyway, but now your IT department gets to figure out what happens when your browser extension can autonomously click around your systems.

ai-at-work.title: Apple sues OpenAI, former employees over alleged intellectual property theft
ai-at-work.excerpt: Apple Inc. today sued OpenAI Group PBC for allegedly stealing intellectual property related to its consumer devices. The iPhone maker filed the complaint with the U.S. District Court for the Northern
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Apple is suing OpenAI for allegedly stealing IP related to consumer devices, particularly around technology acquired when OpenAI bought io Products, a startup founded by ex-Apple executives. This matters because it signals that major tech players are getting serious about protecting their intellectual property in the AI era, and it's a reminder that poaching talent and then commercializing similar products in new markets is increasingly risky business. Honestly, this feels less like surprising news and more like the inevitable collision between two companies playing in overlapping sandboxes, except one of them is now angry about the toys the other company walked away with.

tools-tech.title: I ditched Google Drive for my own self-hosted storage - and I wish I'd done it sooner
tools-tech.excerpt: Nextcloud is a free and open-source storage option that offers several advantages. Here's how it works.
tools-tech.dwp_take: A tech writer moved from Google Drive to self-hosted Nextcloud storage and found it worth the switch. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because it highlights the real tension between convenience and control, especially for organizations that need tighter data governance or can't stomach vendor lock-in. Look, self-hosting isn't magic and it requires actual competence to maintain properly, but the fact that someone's singing its praises tells you that cloud commodification has gotten expensive enough to make the friction worthwhile again.

tools-tech.title: The 'learn to code' era is over - and employers are on the hook for reskilling now
tools-tech.excerpt: AI's ushered in a new era of reskilling. Here's what the industry can learn from the last decade's drive to put people in tech jobs.
tools-tech.dwp_take: The tech industry's "learn to code" movement, which promised anyone could jump into programming, has proven insufficient as AI reshapes skill requirements faster than bootcamps can adapt. Digital workplace leaders now face real pressure to build internal reskilling programs because the old model of expecting workers to figure it out on their own simply didn't stick. Frankly, companies that spent the last decade saying "go get trained on your own time" are about to discover that retaining institutional knowledge beats recruiting from a dried-up talent pool, but good luck explaining that to the CFO.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft Exchange Server on prem gets a little harder to use
tools-tech.excerpt: It’s the end of the road for yet another facet of Exchange Server, Microsoft’s on-premises email and calendar system. The stripped-down version of its web client, Outlook Web App (OWA) Light, is being
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft is discontinuing OWA Light, the stripped-down version of Outlook Web App for on-premises Exchange Server, forcing users onto the standard OWA interface. This matters because it's yet another push from Microsoft eliminating legacy options, which means IT teams managing hybrid or on-prem Exchange environments have fewer choices and less flexibility for users with older browsers or limited bandwidth. After 30 years in this space, I'll say it plainly: Microsoft keeps making on-prem look worse to drive cloud migration, which works great for Microsoft's bottom line but leaves plenty of organizations with valid reasons for staying on-prem stuck with increasingly clunky options.

tools-tech.title: Mistral joins rush to build physical AI
tools-tech.excerpt: French AI company Mistral claims its latest AI model offers a more efficient way to train and operate robots. The model, Robostral Navigate, can guide a robot through plain language instructions, usin
tools-tech.dwp_take: Mistral rolled out an AI model designed to control robots using just plain language commands and a basic camera, ditching the expensive sensor arrays most competitors rely on. This matters because if it actually works as promised, it could make intelligent robotics accessible to organizations without deep pockets or IT departments already stretched thin managing your everyday collaboration tools. That said, I've seen plenty of "simpler, cheaper AI" announcements turn into "works great in demos, nightmare in your actual warehouse" situations, so let's see how Robostral Navigate performs when it's doing real work instead of impressing investors.

digital-culture.title: Kaiser nurses say AI is changing their jobs—for the worse
digital-culture.excerpt: In 2024, hundreds of nurses gathered outside a Kaiser Permanente hospital in San Francisco, carrying signs that read: “Trust nurses, not AI.” As the nurses union started contract negotiations last yea
digital-culture.dwp_take: Kaiser nurses walked out over AI tools that are making their jobs harder instead of easier, with the union demanding better protections around how these systems get deployed in patient care. This matters because it's a real-world test case of what happens when organizations rush to adopt AI without actually asking the people doing the work what problems it creates. Here's the thing: if you can't get nurses on board with your AI implementation, you've already lost, because they're the ones who actually know what matters on the job.

digital-culture.title: LinkedIn is the ‘most AI-saturated platform,’ new study suggests
digital-culture.excerpt: The amount of AI-generated content you scroll through might be far greater than you think, according to a new study by the AI detection platform Pangram. Pangram asked users of its Chrome extension to
digital-culture.dwp_take: LinkedIn's AI detection study found that the platform is drowning in machine-generated content, with Pangram's tool identifying significantly more AI posts than most users realize. This matters because digital workplace professionals rely on LinkedIn for industry insights, networking, and recruiting, but if you can't trust what you're reading, you're essentially scrolling through an elaborate game of content bingo. After thirty years watching communication platforms evolve, I'll say this: LinkedIn becoming an AI farm is peak irony for a platform built on "authentic professional connection."

digital-culture.title: Is our whole model of leadership wrong?
digital-culture.excerpt: My husband and I stumbled into Imago therapy early in our marriage. We were both open to therapy because we knew enough to know what we didn’t know. He came from a divorce, and I came from witnessing
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company ran a piece exploring whether traditional leadership models are fundamentally flawed, using Imago therapy as a lens for rethinking how leaders communicate and relate to their teams. The real insight isn't that therapy is the answer, it's that leaders who actually listen instead of broadcast tend to get better results, which shouldn't surprise anyone but apparently still does.

digital-culture.title: OpenAI’s Head of Safety Is Leaving the Company
digital-culture.excerpt: Johannes Heidecke’s departure comes as OpenAI tries to further integrate its research and safety teams.
digital-culture.dwp_take: OpenAI's head of safety, Johannes Heidecke, is leaving the company as it consolidates its research and safety operations into one unit. This matters to digital workplace pros because it signals how AI companies are structuring governance around emerging tech, which directly impacts how organizations will eventually adopt and manage these tools internally. Honestly, integrating safety into general research sounds nice in theory, but history suggests that when you fold oversight into product teams, safety usually loses the tug of war that follows.

industry-news.title: Apple Wallet Car Key Support Could Expand to Lucid, Xiaomi Vehicles
industry-news.excerpt: iOS 27 beta code hints that Lucid and Xiaomi vehicles could gain Apple Car Key support, though compatible models and launch timing remain unconfirmed. The post Apple Wallet Car Key Support Could Expan
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple's adding Lucid and Xiaomi vehicles to its digital car key ecosystem in iOS 27, though actual launch dates are still fuzzy. industry-news.title: Claude Code Espionage Campaign Exposes a New Enterprise AI Risk

industry-news.title: Massive Telstra Outage Hits Mobile Networks, Rail, and Payments in Australia
industry-news.excerpt: A Telstra software defect disrupted mobile services, rail communications, payments, and emergency calls across Australia, exposing infrastructure risks. The post Massive Telstra Outage Hits Mobile Net
industry-news.dwp_take: A software bug at Telstra, Australia's largest telco, took down mobile networks, rail systems, payment processing, and emergency services across the country.
